small_guidance:
- The hot GEMM loop has no masking and K=8192, N=8192 are clean multiples — push BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64 with num_warps=8, num_stages=4 to maximize K-loop overlap. Also try BLOCK_N=256 to reduce the partial-max NB and shrink the second-pass work.
- Transpose weight once to (K, N) contiguous so the inner load on B is along the contiguous K axis with unit stride; this eliminates strided W loads in the hot loop and typically gives 10-20% on 4090.
- Fuse the final cross-tile max reduction into the GEMM by writing a single persistent kernel where each program handles one row tile across all N tiles, accumulating row-max in registers — this removes the partial buffer and the second kernel launch entirely.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a single-pass split-K-free persistent kernel: one program per row-tile of BLOCK_M rows, looping over all N tiles in registers, maintaining a running row-wise max. Since the post-max math collapses to zero (mean of a length-1 row), the kernel can store zeros directly after computing (and using) the max — avoiding the partial materialization and the second reduction kernel.
- Alternative: keep two-stage but make stage-1 a streaming-K GEMM that emits per-(row, n-tile) max only (no full acc materialized to memory); and fuse stage-2 into the same launch via an atomic-max on a (M,) scratch with a sentinel -inf init. This trades atomics for one fewer kernel launch and zero intermediate (M, NB) buffer.
- Consider tf32 on `tl.dot` (allow_tf32=True) and weight pre-transpose at __init__ time stored as a buffer — this is a one-time layout change that benefits every forward.
